question.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral 

$$
{∬}_{S}12xyz\,\text{d}S
$$

where $S$ is defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=g(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f(x,y,z)$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

For the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂x}=\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+y)=1,
$$

and

$$
\frac{∂z}{∂y}=\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+y)=1.
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be evaluated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}12xyz\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(x,y,g(x,y))\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,12xy(x+y)\sqrt{1+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,12xy(x+y)\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{D}\,12{x}^{2}y+12x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(12{x}^{2}y+12x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}[6{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+4x{y}^{3}]_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(6{x}^{2}+4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\sqrt{3}\,[2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}(2+2)-0 \\  & =4\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
